reranked_evidence.title: The Geography of JAMMU & KASHMIR
reranked_evidence.snippet:
The Geography of JAMMU & KASHMIR
Harshit Rautela
229000 subscribers
7346 likes
348994 views
1 Jun 2025
This video describes the physical and political geography of the Himalayan territory of Jammu and Kashmir in India (including Pakistan occupied Kashmir as well). The beautiful state, with high Himalayas in Kishtwar and vast valley of Kashmir, from beautiful grasslands (margs) in Pir Panjal and Shamsbari to undulating Shivalik and plains of Jammu, this union territory and future state of India has a lot to offer. Jammu and Kashmir has countless water springs, called Nags, like Kokernag and Verinag, the largest city of Himalayas, Srinagar, and the fertile plains of Jammu in the south. India's largest freshwater Lake (Wular), longest Road tunnel (Chenani-Nashri on NH-44) and longest railway tunnel (T-50 on USBRL), as well as highest railway and highest arch bridge (Chenab Railway Bridge) are here.
This video describes the state in three major ways, political geography, using its mountain ranges, and using its rivers and their basins.
It will get complex, serious people might want to keep a notebook, or google earth handy, but, as always, enjoy!

reranked_evidence.title: My Jammu - Jammu City Portal
reranked_evidence.snippet: Amidst the captivating embrace of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, there lies a gem of a city known as Jammu. A cherished winter capital, it proudly wears the crown of being the headquarters and the largest city in the Jammu district. Nestled alongside the flowing river Tawi, it spans an enchanting area of 240 kms, caressed by the grandeur of the Himalayas in the north and embraced by the serenity of the northern plains in the south. As the second-most populous city in the union territory, Jammu weaves its spell on all who grace its sacred soil. Dancing to the rhythm of a glorious heritage, Jammu is hailed as the "City of Temples," enchanting seekers of spirituality and history alike with its ancient temples and shrines. With its eyes set on transformation, Jammu aspires to become a city "of the people, for the people, and by the people," where the dreams of its residents intertwine with the tapestry of its eternal spirit.*.
